items.title: Chinese scientists unveil iron flow battery and zero-emission coal cell

featured_image.name: China: 'World's largest' iron-chromium flow battery set for commercial use

items.description: Two separate research teams from Chinese institutions have announced advances in clean energy technology this month, proposing a near-zero-emission coal fuel cell and unveiling an iron-based flow battery that could reshape large-scale energy storage.

items.title: Adidas shares rise after sub-two-hour marathon record

featured_image.name: 2026 TCS London Marathon - Celebrities

items.description:
Shares of Adidas rose on Monday after athletes wearing the company's new Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 racing shoe delivered a historic performance at the 2026 TCS London Marathon, including the first official sub-two-hour marathon in history.

Kenya's Sabastian Sawe crossed the finish line on Sunday in one hour, 59 minutes and 30 seconds, shattering the previous world record held by the late Kelvin Kiptum by 65 seconds and becoming the first man to break the two-hour barrier in a sanctioned race. Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha finished second in 1:59:41, meaning two men ran under two hours in the same competition. In the women's race, defending champion Tigst Assefa set a new women-only world record of 2:15:41, with the top three women all finishing under 2:16 for the first time in marathon history.[1][2][3]

All three record-setters wore the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3. Adidas shares climbed approximately 1.2% on Monday following the results, according to Reuters.[4][5][6]

items.title: OpenAI, Microsoft end exclusive IP deal in revised pact

featured_image.name: Microsoft says OpenAI is now a competitor in AI and search - CNBC

items.description: OpenAI and Microsoft disclosed an amended partnership agreement on Sunday that removes Microsoft's exclusive rights to OpenAI's intellectual property and allows the AI company to serve customers across any cloud provider, according to The Wall Street Journal. The revised deal grants OpenAI more freedom while capping the revenue share it must pay Microsoft, marking the latest chapter in a relationship that has grown increasingly complex as the AI industry has expanded.[1]

items.title: Iran's Araghchi meets Putin as US peace talks stall

featured_image.name: Iran FM Abbas Araghchi in St Petersburg after 'productive' Pakistan, Oman  diplomacy

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in St. Petersburg on Monday to hold talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, capping an intensive diplomatic tour across Pakistan and Oman as negotiations between Tehran and Washington over the ongoing conflict remain stalled.[1][2][3]

items.title: China blocks Meta's $2B acquisition of AI startup Manus

featured_image.name: Beijing's surprise intervention on Meta's Manus rattles tech ... - CNBC

items.description:
China's top economic planner on Monday ordered the cancellation of Meta Platforms' $2 billion acquisition of artificial intelligence startup Manus, a decisive move to keep homegrown AI technology within Beijing's borders amid an intensifying tech rivalry with the United States.

The National Development and Reform Commission issued a brief statement saying the deal's cancellation was made "in accordance with laws and regulations," according to Bloomberg  and Reuters. The NDRC did not elaborate further. Meta representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment.[1][2]

items.title: Trump warns Iran's oil pipelines could explode within three days

featured_image.name: Trump's Iran ultimatum and signals of a possible deal keep investors ...

items.description: US President Donald Trump warned on Sunday that Iran's oil pipelines could "explode from within" in a matter of days, ratcheting up pressure on Tehran to agree to a ceasefire deal as the two-month-old conflict entered its latest phase of brinkmanship.

items.title: China races to build 2,800-satellite AI network in orbit

featured_image.name: China's in-orbit satellite performs AI large-model tests - CGTN

items.description: China is pushing forward on two fronts in space — a commercial initiative to build a 2,800-satellite AI computing network and a military expansion that U.S. officials warn could challenge American dominance in orbit within the next decade and a half.

items.title: Iran war sends PCB prices surging, squeezing tech firms

featured_image.name: Fire breaks out at Saudi petrochemical complex as strikes target energy  infrastructure

items.description: The Iran war's toll on the global tech supply chain deepened this week as Reuters reported that Iran's early April strike on Saudi Arabia's Jubail petrochemical complex has halted production of high-purity polyphenylene ether (PPE) resin, a critical material used to manufacture the printed circuit board laminates found in virtually every electronic device.[1][2]

items.title: Iran war pushes African, South Asian homes back to charcoal and firewood

featured_image.name: African woman cooking over an open fire in Nigeria, Africa

items.description:
Before sunset in Nairobi's Kibera settlement, Brenda Obare used to cook dinner with a quick turn of her gas stove's knob. Now she crouches over a charcoal burner, coaxing a smoky fire outside her tin-roofed home. "We don't have many options," she told the Associated Press. "You use what you can afford."[1]

Obare's story has become emblematic of a cascading crisis. The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran — which began in late February and led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz — has disrupted roughly 20 percent of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade. As energy prices surged more than 55 percent since the conflict began, the shockwaves have reached the kitchens, forests, and wildlife habitats of Africa and South Asia, threatening years of progress in public health and conservation.[2][3][1]

items.title: Global military spending hit record $2.89 trillion in 2025, SIPRI reports

featured_image.name: Global military spending rise continues as European and Asian ...

items.description: World military expenditure reached $2.887 trillion in 2025, marking the 11th consecutive annual increase and the highest level ever recorded, according to new data released Monday by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI). The 2.9 percent real-terms increase pushed global military spending to 2.5 percent of GDP, its highest share since 2009.[1][2][3]

items.title: Zelenskyy says EU accession talks could open in June

featured_image.name: Ukraine officially begins EU accession negotiations

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that he expects the European Union to formally open the first negotiating clusters for Ukraine's accession talks as soon as June, declaring that Kyiv has fulfilled all the preparatory requirements demanded by Brussels.

"We see approximate dates, maybe in June," Zelenskyy said, according to Liga.net, adding that a decision on the clusters could come between late May and June. The remarks came after a meeting in Kyiv with Moldovan President Maia Sandu, with both leaders pressing the EU to move forward on membership negotiations without further delay.[1][2]

items.title: Hardliner set to replace Ghalibaf in Iran nuclear talks

featured_image.name: Ultra-hardliner who mocked Trump poised to take over nuclear talks

items.description: A confidential letter addressed to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has exposed a rift at the highest levels of power in Tehran, with senior officials warning that the country's economic crisis leaves no choice but to negotiate with the United States over the nuclear issue — a position that directly challenges a red line set by Khamenei himself.

items.title: Iran refuses talks unless US lifts naval blockade

featured_image.name: US Intercepts Iranian ‘Shadow Fleet’ Vessel as Ports Blockade Intensifies

items.description: The US Navy intercepted the sanctioned tanker M/V Sevan in the Arabian Sea on Saturday, forcing the vessel to turn back toward Iran under escort as the American naval blockade of Iranian ports continues to expand. The operation brought the total number of vessels redirected since the blockade began on April 13 to 37.[1][2]

items.title: China quietly expands economic pressure toolkit during trade truce

featured_image.name: Chips and clouds: U.S.-China trade war escalates

items.description:
Even as Washington and Beijing publicly prepare for a mid-May summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, China has been quietly assembling a broad new arsenal of economic countermeasures under cover of the trade truce the two leaders struck last October in Busan, South Korea.

Since that meeting — which Trump rated "a 12 out of 10" — Beijing has enacted sweeping new laws, tightened export controls on critical minerals, banned foreign AI chips from state-funded data centers, barred American and Israeli cybersecurity software from Chinese firms, and begun weighing restrictions on solar manufacturing equipment exports to the United States, according to a Reuters analysis published on Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Chinese scientists create 'predator' material that hunts uranium in water

featured_image.name: Chinese researchers create active material for targeted uranium recovery

items.description: An international research team based in China has created a microscopic material that behaves like a predator, autonomously swimming through water to hunt and capture uranium ions — a development that could reshape nuclear fuel sourcing and radioactive pollution cleanup.

items.title: Zelenskyy says EU loan triggered Russia's 20-hour assault on Dnipro

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy links massive Dnipro attack to $90B EU funding boost | RBC-Ukraine

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that Russia's prolonged missile and drone attack on the city of Dnipro was a direct reaction to the European Union's decision to unblock a €90 billion loan for Ukraine, and announced that three additional countries had pledged €350–400 million to a NATO-backed defense funding program during an EU summit in Cyprus.

items.title: Trump pulls envoys from Pakistan trip for Iran talks

featured_image.name: Trump Cancels Iran Peace Talks at Last Minute - Time Magazine

items.description: President Donald Trump on Saturday abruptly called off a planned trip by his top negotiators to Islamabad for peace talks with Iran, deepening uncertainty over diplomatic efforts to end a conflict now in its third month. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, with mine-clearing operations expected to stretch on for months and the United Nations warning of a looming global hunger crisis.

items.title: Chile's dark skies remain at risk despite energy project cancellation, scientists warn

featured_image.name: Light pollution is threatening the darkest skies on Earth. Here's how ...

items.description:
In one of the driest and darkest places on Earth, astronomers have secured a hard-fought victory to preserve the night sky — but they warn the fight is far from over.

AES Andes, a subsidiary of the U.S. energy company AES Corporation, formally withdrew its proposed INNA green energy project from Chile's Environmental Assessment Service in February, ending a yearlong confrontation between the scientific community and a sprawling industrial development planned just 10 kilometers from the European Southern Observatory's Paranal Observatory in the Atacama Desert.[1][2]

items.title: US orders global diplomatic push over alleged Chinese AI theft

featured_image.name: Where is DeepSeek AI Located? HQ, Global Offices & Company Insights

items.description:
The United States State Department has ordered a worldwide diplomatic campaign warning allies about what Washington describes as systematic efforts by Chinese firms to steal American artificial intelligence technology, according to a diplomatic cable first reported by Reuters on Friday.[1][2]

The cable, dated 25 April and sent to diplomatic and consular posts globally, instructs staff to raise with foreign counterparts "concerns over adversaries' extraction and distillation of US AI models". It names DeepSeek, alongside Chinese firms Moonshot AI and MiniMax, and states that a separate demarche has been sent to Beijing for direct engagement with Chinese officials.[3][4][5]

items.title: Trump cancels Iran peace talks as U.S. naval blockade enters third week

featured_image.name: Scoop: Trump convenes Iran situation room meeting amid renewed Hormuz crisis

items.description: The United States naval blockade of Iran's ports in the Strait of Hormuz has now stretched into its third week with no end in sight, after President Donald Trump on Saturday abruptly canceled planned peace talks and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared the operation will continue "as long as it takes."[1][2]
